results.title: Alternating word
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For elements $a$ and $b$ of a monoid and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the alternating word of length $n$ starting with $a$ is the product $a b a b \cdots$ of $n$ factors that alternate between $a$ and $b$, beginning with $a$; for $n = 0$ it is the identity.

results.title: Monoid homomorphisms preserve alternating words
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f : G \to H$ be a homomorphism of monoids. For all $a, b \in G$ and $n \in \mathbb{N}$, $f$ maps the alternating word $a b a \cdots$ of length $n$ starting with $a$ to the alternating word $f(a) f(b) f(a) \cdots$ of length $n$ starting with $f(a)$.

results.title: Artin relator
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $M = (m_{ij})$ be a Coxeter matrix over an index type $B$, and write $s_i$ for the free generators of the free group on $B$. The Artin relator of the ordered pair $(i, j)$ is the element $u v^{-1}$ of the free group; setting it equal to $1$ imposes the braid relation $u = v$.

results.caption: Definition

results.title: Hall subgroup (Kourovka Problem 19.109)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a Hall subgroup when its order $|H|$ is coprime to its index $|G : H|$, where an infinite order or index is counted as $0$.

results.title: Pronormal subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is pronormal in $G$ when for every $g \in G$ there is an element $x$ of the subgroup $\langle H, gHg^{-1} \rangle$ generated by $H$ and $gHg^{-1}$ such that $xHx^{-1} = gHg^{-1}$.

results.title: Second maximal subgroup
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $K$ of a group $G$ is second maximal when it is a maximal subgroup of a maximal subgroup of $G$: there is a maximal subgroup $M$ of $G$ with $K < M$ and no subgroup $L$ of $G$ with $K < L < M$.

results.title: Zenkov's question on Hall maximal subgroups (Kourovka Problem 19.109)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For every non-abelian finite simple group $G$, all maximal subgroups of $G$ are Hall subgroups if and only if every second maximal subgroup of $G$ is pronormal in $G$.

results.title: Negative answer to Zenkov's question (Kourovka Problem 19.109)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: It is not true that for every non-abelian finite simple group $G$, all maximal subgroups of $G$ are Hall subgroups if and only if every second maximal subgroup of $G$ is pronormal in $G$.

results.title: Hall subgroup (Kourovka 17.92)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A subgroup $H$ of a group $G$ is a Hall subgroup when its order $|H|$ is coprime to its index $|G : H|$.

results.title: Composition factor of a group (Kourovka 17.92)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For groups $G$ and $S$, $S$ is a composition factor of $G$ when there are subgroups $H$ and $K$ of $G$ such that $H$ is subnormal in $G$, $H \cap K$ is normal in $H$, and the quotient $H/(H \cap K)$ is a simple group isomorphic to $S$.

results.title: Non-soluble groups with Hall maximal subgroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ has this property when $G$ is not soluble and every maximal subgroup of $G$ is a Hall subgroup.

results.title: Kourovka 17.92, first half: the possible composition factors
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The proposition that every non-abelian composition factor of a finite non-soluble group all of whose maximal subgroups are Hall subgroups is isomorphic to $L_2(7)$, $L_2(11)$ or $L_5(2)$. Here $L_n(q)$ is the projective special linear group $\mathrm{PSL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})$, the quotient of $\mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/q\mathbb{Z})$ by its centre.

results.title: Kourovka 17.92, second half: the three factors occur

results.title: Maslova's theorem on groups with Hall maximal subgroups

results.title: Linear asymptotic Dirichlet continuation

results.title: Root count
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$, $a \in \mathbb{C}$ and real $r$, the root count of $f$ at $a$ in radius $r$ is the number of roots of $f(z) = a$ in the open disk $|z| < r$, counted with multiplicity: the sum over $z \in \mathbb{C}$ of the positive part of the divisor of $f - a$ on that disk at $z$ (the sum is taken to be $0$ if infinitely many terms are nonzero).

results.title: Maximum valence
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and real $r$, $n(f, r)$ is the supremum in $\mathbb{R}$, over all $a \in \mathbb{C}$, of the root count of $f$ at $a$ in radius $r$, that is, of the number of roots of $f(z) = a$ in $|z| < r$ counted with multiplicity.

results.title: Spherical density
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and $z \in \mathbb{C}$, the spherical density of $f$ at $z$ is $|f'(z)|^2 / (1 + |f(z)|^2)^2$, where $f'(z)$ is the complex derivative of $f$ at $z$, taken to be $0$ where $f$ is not differentiable.

results.title: Normalized spherical area
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ and real $r$, the normalized spherical area $A(f, r)$ of $f$ on the disk $|z| < r$ is $\frac{1}{\pi}$ times the Lebesgue integral of the spherical density of $f$ over the open disk $\{z \in \mathbb{C} : |z| < r\}$ (the integral is taken to be $0$ if the density is not integrable there).

results.title: Germ-wise nonconstant function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ is nonconstant if there are points $u, v \in \mathbb{C}$ at which $f$ is complex differentiable and $f(u) \ne f(v)$.

results.title: Bounded root counts
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ has bounded root counts if for every real $r$ the root counts of $f$ in radius $r$, that is, the numbers of roots of $f(z) = a$ in $|z| < r$ counted with multiplicity, are bounded above as $a$ ranges over $\mathbb{C}$.

results.title: Hayman's spherical-area ratio conjecture is false
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Not every function $f\colon \mathbb{C} \to \mathbb{C}$ that is meromorphic on all of $\mathbb{C}$ and nonconstant (complex differentiable at two points where it takes different values) has bounded root counts and satisfies $\liminf_{r \to \infty} n(f, r)/A(f, r) = 1$, where $n(f, r)$ is the maximum valence and $A(f, r)$ the normalized spherical area of $f$ on the disk $|z| < r$.

results.title: Boolean cube
results.caption: Abbreviation
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ is the set of functions $x : \{0, \dots, n-1\} \to \{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$. It represents $\{-1, 1\}^n$, with true standing for $1$ and false for $-1$.

results.title: Sign of a Boolean coordinate
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The sign of a Boolean value $b$ is the real number $\sigma(b)$ given by $\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$ and $\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$.

results.title: Fourier character on the Boolean cube
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a set $S$ of coordinates among $n$, the Fourier character $\chi_S$ is the real-valued function on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates given by $\chi_S(x) = \prod_{i \in S} \sigma(x_i)$, where $\sigma$ is the sign of a coordinate: $\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$ and $\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$.

results.title: Fourier coefficient on the Boolean cube
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, a function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$ and a set $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the normalized Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$ is $\hat f(S) = \frac{1}{|\{-1, 1\}^n|} \sum_{x \in \{-1, 1\}^n} f(x) \chi_S(x)$, where $\chi_S(x) = \prod_{i \in S} x_i$. That is, $\hat f(S)$ is the uniform expectation of $f \chi_S$.

results.title: Fourier degree at most $d$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A real-valued function $f$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ has Fourier degree at most a natural number $d$ when its Fourier coefficient $\hat f(S)$ vanishes for every set $S$ of coordinates with $|S| > d$.

results.title: Sign of true
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The sign $\sigma(\text{true})$ of the Boolean value true equals $1$.

results.title: Sign of false
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The sign $\sigma(\text{false})$ of the Boolean value false equals $-1$.

results.title: Coordinate signs square to one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every Boolean value $b$, its sign $\sigma(b)$ satisfies $\sigma(b) \cdot \sigma(b) = 1$.

results.title: The empty Fourier character is constant one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n$ and every point $x$ of the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, the Fourier character $\chi_\emptyset$ of the empty set of coordinates satisfies $\chi_\emptyset(x) = 1$.

results.title: Singleton Fourier characters are coordinate signs
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n$, every coordinate $i$ and every point $x$ of the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, the Fourier character $\chi_{\{i\}}$ of the singleton $\{i\}$ satisfies $\chi_{\{i\}}(x) = \sigma(x_i)$, where $\sigma$ is the sign of a coordinate: $\sigma(\text{true}) = 1$ and $\sigma(\text{false}) = -1$.

results.title: Fourier characters square to one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n$, every set $S$ of the $n$ coordinates and every point $x$ of the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, the Fourier character $\chi_S$ satisfies $\chi_S(x) \cdot \chi_S(x) = 1$.

results.title: The empty Fourier coefficient is the mean
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every function $f : \{-1, 1\}^n \to \mathbb{R}$, the normalized Fourier coefficient of $f$ at the empty set is the uniform mean of $f$: $\hat f(\emptyset) = \frac{1}{|\{-1, 1\}^n|} \sum_{x \in \{-1, 1\}^n} f(x)$.

results.title: Fourier coefficients of the zero function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the normalized Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the identically zero function on $\{-1, 1\}^n$ is $0$.

results.title: A character's own Fourier coefficient
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $S \subseteq \{0, \dots, n-1\}$, the normalized Fourier coefficient at $S$ of the character $\chi_S(x) = \prod_{i \in S} x_i$ on $\{-1, 1\}^n$ equals $1$, that is, $\widehat{\chi_S}(S) = 1$.

results.title: Empty Fourier coefficient of a constant function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every real $c$, the normalized Fourier coefficient at the empty set of the constant function $x \mapsto c$ on the Boolean cube $\{-1, 1\}^n$ equals $c$. This includes dimension $n = 0$.

results.title: The zero function satisfies every Fourier degree bound
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For all natural numbers $n$ and $d$, the zero function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ has Fourier degree at most $d$.

results.title: Fourier degree bounds are monotone
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and let $d \le e$ be natural numbers. If $f$ has Fourier degree at most $d$, then $f$ has Fourier degree at most $e$.

results.title: Fourier degree is at most the dimension
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and let $d \ge n$ be a natural number. Then $f$ has Fourier degree at most $d$.

results.title: Lagrange basis polynomial of a cube point
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $x$ be a point of the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, indexed by $i \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Its cube basis polynomial is the real polynomial $\prod_{i=0}^{n-1} \ell_i$ in the variables $X_0, \dots, X_{n-1}$, where $\ell_i = X_i$ if $x_i$ is true and $\ell_i = 1 - X_i$ if $x_i$ is false. Reading true as $1$ and false as $0$, it is the Lagrange basis polynomial of $x$ on the grid $\{0,1\}^n$.

results.title: Multilinear extension
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f$ be a Boolean-valued function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and read each coordinate and each value as $1$ for true and $0$ for false. The real multilinear extension of $f$ is the polynomial in $\mathbb{R}[X_0, \dots, X_{n-1}]$

results.title: Lagrange basis polynomials on the cube are point indicators
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $x$ and $y$ be points of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and identify $y$ with the point of $\{0,1\}^n \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ whose $i$-th coordinate is $1$ when $y_i$ is true and $0$ when it is false. Then the cube basis polynomial of $x$ evaluated at $y$ equals $1$ if $x = y$ and $0$ otherwise.

results.title: The multilinear extension agrees with its function on the cube
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and let $y$ be a point of the cube, identified with the point of $\{0,1\}^n \subseteq \mathbb{R}^n$ whose $i$-th coordinate is $1$ when $y_i$ is true and $0$ when it is false. Then the real multilinear extension of $f$ evaluated at $y$ equals $1$ if $f(y)$ is true and $0$ if $f(y)$ is false.

results.title: Multilinear extension of a constant function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$ and every Boolean value $b$, the real multilinear extension of the constant function $b$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ is the constant polynomial $1$ if $b$ is true and the constant polynomial $0$ if $b$ is false.

results.title: Multilinear extension of a coordinate projection
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every coordinate $i$ of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, the real multilinear extension of the projection $x \mapsto x_i$ is the variable $X_i$.

results.title: Boolean degree
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $f$ be a Boolean-valued function on the Boolean cube in $n$ coordinates, and read true as $1$ and false as $0$. The Boolean degree of $f$ is the total degree of the multilinear extension of $f$: the real multilinear polynomial in $n$ variables that takes the value $f(x)$ at every point $x \in \{0,1\}^n$.

results.title: Constant functions have Boolean degree zero
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every Boolean value $b$, the constant function $x \mapsto b$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ has Boolean degree $0$.

results.title: Coordinate projections have Boolean degree one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$ and every $i < n$, the coordinate projection $x \mapsto x_i$ on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ has Boolean degree $1$.

results.title: All-true function
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the all-true function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ is the Boolean AND of all coordinates: it sends $x = (x_0, \dots, x_{n-1})$ to true exactly when $x_i$ is true for every $i < n$. In dimension $0$ it is constantly true.

results.title: Multilinear extension of the AND function
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every natural number $n$, the real multilinear extension of the AND function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ (true exactly when every coordinate is true) is the monomial $\prod_{i=0}^{n-1} X_i$.

results.title: The two-bit AND has Boolean degree two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The all-true function on the Boolean cube of dimension $2$, $(x_0, x_1) \mapsto x_0 \wedge x_1$, has Boolean degree $2$; that is, its real multilinear extension has total degree $2$.

results.title: Fourier degree is at most Boolean degree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f$ be a Boolean function on the Boolean cube of dimension $n$, and let $g$ be the real function with $g(x) = 1$ if $f(x)$ is true and $g(x) = 0$ otherwise. Then $g$ has Fourier degree at most the Boolean degree of $f$: every Fourier coefficient $\hat g(S)$ with $|S|$ greater than the total degree of the multilinear extension of $f$ vanishes.

results.title: Fourier character on finite sets
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For finite sets $S$ and $T$, the Fourier character of $S$ at $T$ is the real number $\chi_S(T) = (-1)^{|S \cap T|}$.

results.title: Number of points of the Boolean cube
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every $n \in \mathbb{N}$, the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ has exactly $2^n$ points.

results.title: Subsets of a finite set as indicator functions
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $E$, this is the bijection from the subsets $T \subseteq E$ to the functions $b$ from $E$ to $\{\mathrm{true}, \mathrm{false}\}$ given by $b(a) = \mathrm{false}$ if $a \in T$ and $b(a) = \mathrm{true}$ if $a \notin T$. Its inverse sends $b$ to the set $\{a \in E : b(a) = \mathrm{false}\}$.

results.title: Subsets of a finite set as points of the Boolean cube
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a finite set $E$ with $n = |E|$ elements, fix a bijection $e$ from $E$ to $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (an enumeration of $E$, chosen noncanonically). This is the bijection from the subsets $T \subseteq E$ to the Boolean cube of dimension $n$ that sends $T$ to the point $x$ with $x_{e(a)} = \mathrm{false}$ if $a \in T$ and $x_{e(a)} = \mathrm{true}$ if $a \notin T$, for every $a \in E$.

results.title: Coordinates of an encoded subset
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $E$ be a finite set with $m$ elements, listed in the fixed order $e_0, \dots, e_{m-1}$ used to encode subsets of $E$ as points of the Boolean cube of dimension $m$. For every subset $T \subseteq E$ and every coordinate $j < m$, the $j$-th coordinate of the point encoding $T$ is true if $e_j \notin T$ and false if $e_j \in T$.

results.title: Reindexing a subset as a set of coordinates
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For finite sets $S \subseteq E$ with $n = |E|$, let $e$ be the fixed bijection from $E$ to $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ (the enumeration of $E$ used to identify subsets of $E$ with points of the Boolean cube of dimension $n$). The reindexed set is the image $e(S) = \{e(a) : a \in S\}$, a subset of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$.

results.title: Decoding a cube point as a subset

results.title: Generalized Büchi automaton
results.caption: Structure
results.summary: A generalized Büchi automaton with states $S$ and symbols $\Sigma$ is a nondeterministic automaton (a labelled transition relation on $S$ together with a set of start states) equipped with a natural number $k$ and $k$ acceptance sets $F_0, \dots, F_{k-1} \subseteq S$. A run is accepting when it visits every acceptance set infinitely often.

results.title: Language of a generalized Büchi automaton
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: An infinite word $x$ belongs to the language of a generalized Büchi automaton $g$ with acceptance sets $F_0, \dots, F_{k-1}$ iff there is a run $s$ of $g$ on $x$ such that for every $j < k$ there are infinitely many times $t$ with $s_t \in F_j$. Here a run of $g$ on $x$ is an infinite sequence of states $s_0, s_1, \dots$ with $s_0$ a start state and a transition from $s_i$ to $s_{i+1}$ labelled $x_i$ for every $i$.

results.title: Counter update for degeneralization
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $g$ be a generalized Büchi automaton with acceptance sets $F_0, \dots, F_{k-1}$. The counter update takes a counter value $i \in \{0, \dots, k\}$ and a state $t$ of $g$ and returns a counter value in $\{0, \dots, k\}$: if $i < k$, it returns $i + 1$ when $t \in F_i$ and $i$ when $t \notin F_i$; if $i = k$, it returns $0$.

results.title: The degeneralization counter advances on a hit
results.caption: Theorem
